From 6cc4a0863c9709c512280c64e698d68443ac8053 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: Manjunath Patil <manjunath.b.patil@oracle.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Oct 2018 09:49:21 -0700
Subject: [PATCH] xen-blkfront: fix kernel panic with negotiate_mq error path
MIME-Version: 1.0
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8
Content-Transfer-Encoding: 8bit

info->nr_rings isn't adjusted in case of ENOMEM error from
negotiate_mq(). This leads to kernel panic in error path.

Typical call stack involving panic -
 #8 page_fault at ffffffff8175936f
    [exception RIP: blkif_free_ring+33]
    RIP: ffffffffa0149491  RSP: ffff8804f7673c08  RFLAGS: 00010292
 ...
 #9 blkif_free at ffffffffa0149aaa [xen_blkfront]
 #10 talk_to_blkback at ffffffffa014c8cd [xen_blkfront]
 #11 blkback_changed at ffffffffa014ea8b [xen_blkfront]
 #12 xenbus_otherend_changed at ffffffff81424670
 #13 backend_changed at ffffffff81426dc3
 #14 xenwatch_thread at ffffffff81422f29
 #15 kthread at ffffffff810abe6a
 #16 ret_from_fork at ffffffff81754078

Cc: stable@vger.kernel.org
Fixes: 7ed8ce1c5fc7 ("xen-blkfront: move negotiate_mq to cover all cases of new VBDs")
Signed-off-by: Manjunath Patil <manjunath.b.patil@oracle.com>
Acked-by: Roger Pau Monné <roger.pau@citrix.com>
Signed-off-by: Juergen Gross <jgross@suse.com>

diff --git a/drivers/block/xen-blkfront.c b/drivers/block/xen-blkfront.c
index 9eea83ae01c6..9ac3999a55b7 100644
--- a/drivers/block/xen-blkfront.c
+++ b/drivers/block/xen-blkfront.c
@@ -1919,6 +1919,7 @@ static int negotiate_mq(struct blkfront_info *info)
 			      GFP_KERNEL);
 	if (!info->rinfo) {
 		xenbus_dev_fatal(info->xbdev, -ENOMEM, "allocating ring_info structure");
+		info->nr_rings = 0;
 		return -ENOMEM;
 	}
 
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `drivers/block/xen-blkfront.c`**
- A new line was added in the `negotiate_mq` function to set `info->nr_rings` to `0` in the case of an `ENOMEM` error when allocating the `rinfo` structure. This change ensures that the `nr_rings` variable is properly adjusted to prevent a kernel panic during error handling.

### Relationships
The modification addresses a specific bug related to the handling of memory allocation failures in the `negotiate_mq` function. By setting `info->nr_rings` to `0` when an `ENOMEM` error occurs, the patch prevents the kernel panic that could arise from using an uninitialized or incorrect value in subsequent operations. This change is directly related to the previous commit identified by the `Fixes` tag, which moved the `negotiate_mq` function to cover all cases of new Virtual Block Devices (VBDs). The patch ensures that the error handling is robust and does not lead to system instability.

Root cause:
The bug occurs because the `info->nr_rings` variable is not adjusted when an `ENOMEM` error is encountered during the allocation of the `rinfo` structure in the `negotiate_mq` function. This oversight leads to the use of an incorrect value in subsequent operations, resulting in a kernel panic.

Code statements information:
The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
info->rinfo = kcalloc(info->nr_rings, sizeof(struct blkfront_ring_info), GFP_KERNEL);
if (!info->rinfo) {
    xenbus_dev_fatal(info->xbdev, -ENOMEM, "allocating ring_info structure");
```
Reason:
The bug occurs because when the `kcalloc` function fails due to an `ENOMEM` error, the `info->nr_rings` variable is not set to zero. This means that subsequent operations may use the incorrect (non-zero) value of `info->nr_rings`, leading to a kernel panic when the code attempts to access or free resources based on this incorrect value.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
info->nr_rings = 0;
return -ENOMEM;
```
Reason:
The fix involves setting `info->nr_rings` to zero when the allocation of `rinfo` fails. This adjustment ensures that any subsequent operations that rely on `info->nr_rings` will not use an invalid value, thus preventing the kernel panic that occurs in the error path.
